newsitem.title: USA: Most expect US rate hike in final pre-FOMC survey.
newsitem.headline: Most expect US rate hike in final pre-FOMC survey.

text.p: A slim majority -- 31 of 55 forecasters surveyed by Reuters -- said Tuesday they expected Federal Reserve policymakers to raise official short-term U.S. interest rates later in the day.

Of the 31 forecasters expecting the Federal Open Market Committee to tighten credit for the first time since February 1, 1995, 20 said policymakers will raise both the 5.25-percent federal funds rate and the 5.0-percent discount rate.
Reuters surveyed 55 U.S. primary dealers, banks and advisory firms.
BZW Government Securities was the only firm calling for an aggressive 50-point move on both benchmark rates on Tuesday.
Scotia Capital was the only other firm expecting a dual 50-point hike on the funds and discount rates -- but not until the next FOMC meeting on November 13.
Two firms -- Salomon Brothers and Morgan Stanley -- said the outcome of the meeting on Tuesday is "too close to call."
The latest Reuters survey showed the market almost evenly divided about the U.S. interest outlook -- as it was in the prior Reuters poll that ran on September 19.

In that survey, 17 of 30 economists and Fed watchers said the Fed is likely to raise short-term interest rates on September 24. All but one -- again, BZW Government Securities -- of the 17 called for a 25 basis point rate hike.
In Tuesday's poll, 13 firms -- including Scotia Capital -- forecast a rate hike on November 13, the first FOMC meeting following the U.S. Presidential elections.
Six firms saw no move this year. Three more did not anticipate a move before 1997 or 1998.
UBS Securities was the only one calling the next Fed move an ease in the first quarter of 1997.
In the latest Reuters survey, 25 new forecasts were added to the 30 that were gathered last Thursday.
